items.title: Νέα Υόρκη: Στα σχολεία της ελληνικής ομογένειας σε Μπρούκλιν και Αστόρια η Σοφία Ζαχαράκη
items.titleOriginal: Νέα Υόρκη: Στα σχολεία της ελληνικής ομογένειας σε Μπρούκλιν και Αστόρια η Σοφία Ζαχαράκη
items.description: Με την ελληνόγλωσση εκπαίδευση στην ομογένεια και τις ε παφές με την αμερικανική πανεπιστημιακή κοινότητα στο επίκεντρο, ολοκληρώνεται σήμερα η πενθήμερη επίσκεψη της υπουργού Παιδείας, Θρησκευμάτων και Αθλητισμού , Σοφίας Ζαχαράκη , στη Νέα Υόρκη . Στο πρόγραμμα της υπουργού περιλαμβάνονταν επαφές με εκπροσώπους του Πανεπιστημίου Columbia, της ελληνόγλωσσης εκπαίδευσης και της ελληνικής…
items.descriptionOriginal: Με την ελληνόγλωσση εκπαίδευση στην ομογένεια και τις ε παφές με την αμερικανική πανεπιστημιακή κοινότητα στο επίκεντρο, ολοκληρώνεται σήμερα η πενθήμερη επίσκεψη της υπουργού Παιδείας, Θρησκευμάτων και Αθλητισμού , Σοφίας Ζαχαράκη , στη Νέα Υόρκη . Στο πρόγραμμα της υπουργού περιλαμβάνονταν επαφές με εκπροσώπους του Πανεπιστημίου Columbia, της ελληνόγλωσσης εκπαίδευσης και της ελληνικής ομογένειας. Την Παρασκευή 20 Νοεμβρίου, η κ. Ζαχαράκη επισκέφθηκε το Hellenic Classical Charter School στο Παρκ Σλοπ του Μπρούκλιν και το Ημερήσιο Λύκειο του Αγίου Δημητρίου στην Αστόρια, όπου συνομίλησε με μαθητές, εκπαιδευτικούς και διευθυντές, καθώς και με εκπαιδευτικούς που υπηρετούν σε ομογενειακά σχολεία. Υποτροφίες και δυνατότητες σπουδών στην Ελλάδα Σε συζήτηση που ακολούθησε με δημοσιογράφους, η υπουργός και η πρόεδρος του Ιδρύματος Κρατικών Υποτροφιών (ΙΚΥ), Βασιλική Κιντή, αναφέρθηκαν στη στήριξη της ομογενειακής εκπαίδευσης από την ελληνική πολιτεία , στον ρόλο των συντονιστών εκπαίδευσης στα Γενικά Προξενεία και στο πρόγραμμα υποτροφιών του ΙΚΥ. Συζητήθηκαν επίσης οι προσπάθειες προσέλκυσης δωρεών και χορηγιών. Στο σκέλος της ανώτατης εκπαίδευσης, ιδιαίτερη αναφορά έγινεστα αγγλόφωνα προγράμματα σπουδών των ελληνικών πανεπιστημίων και στο ενδιαφέρον που εκδηλώνουν ομογενείς για τα προγράμματα των Ιατρικών Σχολών. Η κ. Ζαχαράκη αναφέρθηκε στις προσπάθειες του υπουργείου για την ανακαίνιση και αναβάθμιση υφιστάμενων φοιτητικών εστιών, καθώς και για την ανέγερση νέων, συνολικής δυναμικότητας άνω των 8.000 κλινών. Η υπουργός αναφέρθηκε ακόμη στις εξετάσεις ελληνομάθειας και στο Ψηφιακό Φροντιστήριο, ενώ αντάλλαξε απόψεις με τους δημοσιογράφους για τις προκλήσεις που αντιμετωπίζει το σχολείο του Αγίου Δημητρίου στην Αστόρια. Οι επαφές με την ομογένεια και το μήνυμα προς τους νέους Στο πλαίσιο της επίσκεψης της, η κ. Ζαχαράκη συναντήθηκε στο Γενικό Προξενείο με αντιπροσωπεία της Ομοσπονδίας Ελληνικών Σωματείων Μείζονος Νέας Υόρκης και παραχώρησε συνέντευξη στον ομογενειακό ραδιοφωνικό σταθμό Cosmos FM 91.5. Στη συνέντευξη, με τους Δημήτρη Φίλιο και Στέλιο Τακετζή, η κ. Ζαχαράκη αναφέρθηκε στην προσπάθεια εξεύρεσης πρόσθετων πόρων για υποτροφίες του Ιδρύματος Κρατικών Υποτροφιών (ΙΚΥ) και στη στήριξη της ελληνόγλωσσης εκπαίδευσης στην ομογένεια. Η υπουργός επισήμανε ότ ι οι υποτροφίες μπορούν να καλύψουν έξοδα στέγασης και διαβίωσης , δίνοντας σε νέους με οικονομικές δυσκολίες τη δυνατότητα να σπουδάσουν στην Ελλάδα ή στο εξωτερικό. Η υπουργός κατέταξε την ελληνόγλωσση εκπαίδευση στο εξωτερικό στις πέντε βασικές προτεραιότητες του υπουργείου, δίνοντας έμφαση στην έγκαιρη τοποθέτηση εκπαιδευτικών στα σχολεία και στα τμήματα ελληνικής γλώσσας της ομογένειας. Απευθυνόμενη στους νέους της διασποράς, τους κάλεσε να εξετάσουν τη δυνατότητα σπουδών στην Ελλάδα, αναφερόμενη στα ξενόγλωσσα προγράμματα σπουδών στην Αθήνα, τη Θεσσαλονίκη, την Πάτρα και την Αλεξανδρούπολη. «Κάθε παιδί, όπου και αν έχει γεννηθεί, να μπορέσει να έχει μια ισότιμη πρόσβαση στην εκπαίδευση», ανέφερε η κ. Ζαχαράκη, αναφερόμενη σε μαθητές από ένα μικρό σχολείο στα Άγραφα Ευρυτανίας έως το κέντρο της Αθήνας, καθώς και στα παιδιά της ομογένειας που παρακολουθούν μαθήματα ελληνικών. Περισσότεροι από 750 εκπαιδευτικοί σε σχολεία του εξωτερικού Στις προτεραιότητες του υπουργείου συμπεριέλαβε επίσης τους μόνιμους διορισμούς εκπαιδευτικών , τη βελτίωση του περιεχομένου της διδασκαλίας, την αναβάθμιση των σχολικών υποδομών και τη βελτίωση των συνθηκών φοίτησης στα πανεπιστήμια, μεταξύ άλλων με περισσότερες φοιτητικές εστίες. Η κ. Ζαχαράκη ανέφερε ότι η φετινή υπουργική απόφαση για τις αποσπάσεις εκδόθηκε νωρίτερα από κάθε προηγούμενη χρονιά και δήλωσε ότι το υπουργείο θα επιδιώξει να συνεχίσει την ίδια πρακτική. Όπως εξήγησε, η έγκαιρη έκδοση των αποφάσεων διευκολύνει την τοποθέτηση των εκπαιδευτικών στα σχολεία και στα τμήματα ελληνικής γλώσσας και τους δίνει περισσότερο χρόνο για να διευθετήσουν ζητήματα στέγασης και έκδοσης βίζας. Σύμφωνα με την υπουργό, το υπουργείο έχει αποσπάσει περισσότερους από 750 εκπαιδευτικούς στο εξωτερικό, εκ των οποίων 16 στη Νέα Υόρκη. Πηγή: ΑΠΕ-ΜΠΕ www.ertnews.gr

items.descriptionOriginal: Lockheed Martin has put a new rocket training system through its third successful flight test, moving closer to a potential replacement for the U.S. Army’s existing practice rockets. The demonstration involved firing 24 training rounds from a High Mobility Artillery Rocket System (HIMARS) launcher. The November test took place at Yuma Proving Ground in Arizona. It evaluated the Joint Reduced Range Rocket (JR3), a training system designed to make live-fire exercises more affordable. Its reusable launch hardware could help the Army conduct more frequent rocket drills without relying on expensive operational ammunition. The JR3 program targets U.S. Army requirements and could eventually serve international military partners. Lockheed Martin is developing the system around established rocket motor technology. Its design focuses on reducing the cost of repeated training exercises while retaining realistic firing characteristics. New approach to training Rocket artillery crews need regular live-fire exercises to maintain proficiency. However, training with operational ammunition can place considerable pressure on military budgets. Range availability and ammunition costs also limit how frequently crews can practice. JR3 aims to address those challenges through a purpose-built training round. Its rocket motor uses established technology, helping avoid the expense of developing an entirely new propulsion system. The system also features an adaptable payload that produces visible marking effects. These effects allow instructors to evaluate rocket placement during exercises. The November demonstration examined the rocket’s range, flight path, and accuracy. Lockheed Martin previously conducted another successful JR3 flight test in August. That demonstration involved launching rockets from a HIMARS launcher. The November exercise expanded the testing with a complete 24-round salvo. Reusable launch hardware matters One of JR3’s most interesting engineering features involves its launch infrastructure. The system pairs individual training rounds with a reusable 24-round rocket launch pod. Its reloadable launch tubes allow crews to reuse critical launch hardware across multiple training cycles. That approach could lower the overall expense of maintaining regular live-fire programs. JR3 also supports both HIMARS and M270 Multiple Launch Rocket System launchers. These platforms give the Army flexibility when organizing artillery training across different units. The system’s design also addresses environmental flexibility. Lockheed Martin intends JR3 to support exercises across different locations and operating conditions. Crews could conduct realistic firing drills during daylight or nighttime training sessions. Sabrina Barnes, vice president of Lockheed Martin Precision Fires Rockets, described affordability as a central design priority. “Our new training round offers a scalable, very affordable solution built on mature rocket motor technology,” Barnes said. She added that the 24-round launch pod addresses the Army’s demand for greater training volume. The system aims to deliver that capacity without compromising performance. Future applications beyond training JR3 remains under development, but its modular design could offer applications beyond conventional training exercises. Lockheed Martin says the architecture could support future efforts involving inexpensive, mass-producible rockets. That possibility makes the program relevant beyond its immediate replacement objective. A modular approach could allow developers to adapt existing components for different requirements. However, Lockheed Martin has not announced specific operational applications for such future variants. The Army’s eventual adoption will depend on further development and testing. The three successful demonstrations provide evidence of the system’s flight performance. Further evaluation will determine how effectively JR3 meets military training requirements. Its central proposition remains straightforward: give artillery crews more opportunities to practice without consuming expensive operational rockets. The reusable launch pod and established motor technology form the foundation of that approach.

items.descriptionOriginal: During the 1920s , radios had a boom in the United States. Sales of radios went from $60 million in 1922 to $426 million in 1929, according to the University of Houston Digital History . Families began to gather around their radios and listen to comedies, musical variety shows and news. And the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Bureau of Home Economics and Farm Radio Service decided to create its own 15-minute broadcast aimed at housewives and all things homemaking in a number of different segments. The show, called Housekeeper Chat , centered on the fictional character Aunt Sammy, the wife of Uncle Sam (the famous United State’s federal government persona). It premiered on October 4, 1926. Aunt Sammy’s radio segments, explained The 15-minute Housekeeper Chat show was broken down into three, 5-minute segments: “Backyard Gossip”, “Questions Women are Asking”, and “What Shall We Have For Dinner?”. Real women took on the role of Aunt Sammy, including: Ruth Van DeMan , a home economics specialist who created many of Aunt Sammy’s recipes and menus; Josephine Hemphill , a journalism teacher who graduated from of Kansas State Agricultural College, who wrote many of the conversational scripts; and Fanny Walker Yeatman, who both tested and tasted recipes that were created for the show by the Bureau of Home Economics. Final show approvals were run through another woman, Dr. Louise Stanley, head of the Bureau of Home Economics, before the show aired. Ruth Van DeMan told a newspaper in 1927, “This is no caviar and truffle service for jazz-jaded appetites. We are striving to serve that great substantial class of women who are homemakers. We aim to make the menus simple and balanced.” Aunt Sammy’s Radio Recipes cookbook Housekeeper Chat was a hit. Demand for a cookbook featuring Aunt Sammy’s recipes and menus came flooding in, and the USDA compiled a cookbook that featured 70 favorite menus and 300 recipes from the show into Aunt Sammy’s Radio Recipes . And 100,000 copies of it were distributed between October 1926 and December 1927. In 1927, a million housewives were tuning in to the hit radio show. And the broadcast survived through the Great Depression, and was renamed to Homemaker Chats after 1934. It was discontinued in 1946, according to the University of North Texas . Photograph of Ruth Van DeMan preparing for the broadcast. Photo Courtesy: National Archive A 1931 recipe from ‘Aunt Sammy’s Radio Recipes’ A 1931 copy of Aunt Sammy’s Radio Recipes Revised is available through South Dakota State University . (You can also try making more original recipes shared back in 1927 in Aunt Sammy’s Radio Recipes: The Original 1927 Cookbook and Housekeeper’s Chat .) Here’s how to make an original recipe 1931 created by Ruth Van DeMan and Fanny Walker Yeatman for a seasonal treat, Cranberry Muffins. Cranberry Muffins 1 egg 3/4 cup milk 1/2 teaspoon salt 4 tablespoons melted butter or other fat 2 cups sifted flour 4 teaspoons baking powder 1/4 cup sugar. 1 cup cranberries Beat the egg slightly and add the milk. To the liquid mixture, add the sifted dry ingredients. Roll the berries in two more tablespoons of sugar, and fold into the batter with the melted fat. Do not stir the mixture any more than necessary. Pour into greased muffin pans and bake in a moderately hot oven (400°F.) for about 30 minutes, or until brown. Serve hot. items.title: Πριν η Natalie Imbruglia τραγουδήσει το "Torn", ο τραγουδοποιός του ηχογράφησε μια εκδοχή με πολύ διαφορετική μπουκιά
items.titleOriginal: Before Natalie Imbruglia sang ‘Torn,’ its songwriter recorded a version with a very different bite
items.description: Κανένα soundtrack της δεκαετίας του 1990 δεν θα ήταν πλήρες χωρίς το "Torn" της Natalie Imbruglia. Το επιτυχημένο σινγκλ ήταν ένα από τα μεγαλύτερα τραγούδια της δεκαετίας του '90, καθώς ήταν στην κορυφή των ραδιοφωνικών charts για 11 εβδομάδες. Αναγνωρίζεται ευρέως ως ένα από τα πιο δημοφιλή και πιο επιδραστικά ποπ τραγούδια ποτέ. Το άγκιστρο ήταν πιασάρικο, η αυστραλιανή φωνή της Imbruglia ήταν μοναδική και μολυσματική και οι στίχοι…
items.descriptionOriginal: No soundtrack of the 1990s would be complete without Natalie Imbruglia’s “Torn.” The hit single was one of the biggest songs of the 90s, topping the radio charts for 11 weeks. It’s widely recognized as one of the most popular and influential pop songs ever. The hook was catchy, Imbruglia’s Australian voice was unique and infectious, and the lyrics were relatable to anyone who’d ever been disillusioned or felt alone even inside of a romantic relationship. The song was so popular, in fact, that it charted all over the world. “Torn” was a hit in Canada, Belgium, Denmark, Spain, and more. Truly iconic. Imbruglia’s “Torn” was, surprisingly, a cover What many people don’t realize about the song that immediately evokes all things 90s is that Imbruglia was not the original songwriter or even performer of “Torn.” “Torn” was written by Anne Preven along with Scott Cutler and Phil Thornalley in 1991, a full six years before Imbruglia’s version was released. Preven and Cutler were members of the California rock band Ednaswap. Ednaswap’s version of “Torn” was wildly different from the version many of us have grown to love. Instead of the lighthearted, whimsical music backing the lyrics and a synthetic beat, Ednaswap performed the song with guitars and heavy drums. Preven’s voice brought a completely different flavor to the lyrics, as well, as she infused it with far more grit; giving the song a mood of anger and frustration, along with a little bit of an edge. Even Ednaswap was not the first to record “Torn” Preven and her bandmates, along with Phil Thornalley, wrote “Torn” in 1991 but did not immediately record it. Instead, the song’s first recording went to Danish artist Lis Sørensen in 1993. Her version was a smash hit in Denmark about four years before Imbruglia recorded hers. But wait, the journey of this incredible song was not nearly over yet. Ednaswap finally recorded their own version of the song they wrote, adding it to their 1995 self-titled album. Meanwhile, the song was still busy making its way around the world. In 1996, singer Trine Rein released her own cover of “Torn” on her album Beneath My Skin . Each of these artists brought something a little different to the piece. Unique musical styles, vocal choices, and tones helped transform the meaning of the song for listeners all over the world. Finally, in 1997, Imbruglia’s version took the world by storm and became the international sensation we know today. But the staying power of the song is seen in the fact that it continues to be covered again and again. Bands and artists like Phoebe Bridgers and Neck Deep have put their own spin on “Torn.” And, famously, the band One Direction covered “Torn” for their very first performance on The X Factor , a showing that helped propel them to stardom. Who knew that such a simple, yet beautifully written, song could have such a lasting impact in pop culture all over the globe? 90s culture, even today’s pop music, might have been permanently altered for the better by a little known band and a trio of incredible songwriters. items.description: Ο Δρ Φρανκενστάιν έμαθε με τον δύσκολο τρόπο ότι δεν μπορούσε να συνδυάσει έναν άνθρωπο σύμφωνα με τις προτιμήσεις του. Ενώ αυτό…
items.descriptionOriginal: Dr. Frankenstein learned the hard way that he couldn’t piece together a human to his own liking. But centuries later, it seems that people haven’t quite figured that out. “Frankensteining” is a buzzy term for attempting to mold your significant other into your idea of a perfect partner, rather than embracing their own unique personality. While this version might not be quite as messy as what’s depicted in the Mary Shelley novel, experts agree it doesn’t exactly lead to a healthy relationship. Upworthy spoke with several relationship experts about what “Frankensteining” looks like, why people do it, and how to tell when a desire for change has crossed a line. Here’s what they had to say. What “Frankensteining” looks like As Dr. Karen Stewart, Psy.D. notes, this behavior is “nothing new.” Unrealistic relationship expectations, perfectionism, or a need for control in a relationship can cause someone to fall in love with their partner’s potential rather than who they actually are. “Frankensteining often starts subtly and can even be disguised as love or concern,” she warns, “such as encouraging your partner to dress differently, lose weight, change their social circle, become more ambitious, or adopt your interests.” She adds that “individually, these suggestions may seem harmless, but over time, they can create a dynamic where one partner feels they are constantly being evaluated or corrected.” What “Frankensteining” is not Frankensteining is different from asking that a partner change a specific behavior (example: “Can you text me if you’ll be late?”), which couples communication coach Amber Frazier-Finkelstein notes is “normal.” Conversely, a demand like “I need you to be more ambitious” or “I wish you were more outgoing” is essentially asking a partner “to rewrite who they are.” In other words, there is a difference between asking a partner to treat you well and asking them to be a completely different person. How to spot the difference According to Dr. Natalie Harvey, LPC-S , a licensed therapist, a good way to tell if you’re “Frankensteining” in a relationship is to ask yourself three questions: Am I responding to who this person is, or to who I need them to be so I feel secure? Have they asked me for this input? If they never changed in this area, would I honestly stay? “It is kinder to accept someone as they are, or to leave honestly, than to stay and redesign them,” she added. Additionally, if you suspect your partner is “Frankensteining” you, Dr. Stewart says you can reflect on these questions: Do I feel supported in who I am currently, and what would it be like if I didn’t make these changes? What does it feel like when I say no to their suggestions? Ultimately, a healthy relationship doesn’t require either person to become someone else. People can grow together, compromise, and work on behaviors that affect the relationship. But again, there’s a big difference between supporting someone’s growth and trying to rebuild them in your own image. And if the person you’re with consistently falls short of the version you’ve imagined in your head, that may be worth paying attention to. Sometimes the more loving choice isn’t figuring out how to change someone. It’s recognizing that they’re already a whole person, and deciding whether the person they are is the person you want to love. The post People are ‘Frankensteining’ their partners. Therapists explain what that actually means. appeared first on Upworthy .

Εκτός κι αν είστε η Έλα Φιτζέραλντ, που μετέτρεψε μια όψεις επί σκηνής σε βραβευμένο θρίαμβο. Ο εμβληματικός τραγουδιστής της τζαζ ανέβηκε στη σκηνή στο Βερολίνο της Γερμανίας, στις 13 Φεβρουαρίου 1960.…
items.descriptionOriginal: Standing on stage in front of a crowd is already terrifying for many people. But being in the spotlight, with all eyes on you, and making a big mistake? Total nightmare fuel. Unless you’re Ella Fitzgerald, who turned an on-stage oopsies into an award-winning triumph. The iconic jazz singer took the stage in Berlin, Germany , on February 13, 1960, to sing “Mack the Knife.” But partway through the song, she completely blanked on the lyrics. She didn’t miss a beat Did Ella panic? Nope. She just kept right on singing the tune with the first words that came to her head: Oh, what’s the next chorus to this song now? This is the one now, I don’t know But it was a swingin’ tune and it’s a hit soon So we tried to do Mack the Knife She kept going in this improvised fashion for nearly two minutes, conjuring lyrics out of thin air. The most impressive part was that the words not only matched the tune and rhythm of the song, but many of them even fit the rhyme scheme. She even joked about her own flub-up within the impromptu lyrics, referencing Bobby Darin and Louis Armstrong, who originally made the song popular: Oh, Bobby Darin and Louis Armstrong They made a record, oh, but they did And now Ella, Ella and her fellas We’re makin’ a wreck, what a wreck of Mack the Knife That live flub-up won her a Grammy Ella Fitzgerald was a global sensation at this point in her career, so maybe audiences would have forgiven the hiccup even if she’d stopped and restarted the song. But the fact that she didn’t skip a beat simply solidified her status as a musical icon. Of course, it also helps that she was a jazz singer. In addition to the freestyle lyrics, she also filled the parts of the song where she had no words with nonsense syllables, a jazz technique known as scatting. Ella was famous for that kind of improvisation. The audience got a kick out of the performance, and the live recording of the song ended up earning her a Grammy for Best Female Vocal Performance (Single) in 1961. She also won Best Vocal Performance Album (Female) for the Mack the Knife—Ella in Berlin album. What made Ella Fitzgerald such a legend Ella Fitzgerald’s voice was nothing if not unique. But her voice didn’t just stand out for its unique sound. She could sing three full octaves (well above average, even for trained singers), and her voice has been described as “flexible, wide-ranging, accurate and ageless.” She could imitate every instrument in the orchestra, and she sang alongside the world’s greatest jazz musicians. Her audience was equally wide-ranging. She sang everywhere from small venues early in her career to world-renowned opera houses as she rose to global fame. People of all ages, races, and nationalities, rich or poor, loved to hear her sing. While she was somewhat self-conscious and reserved in her private life, she was fearless when she took the stage. “Once up there, I felt the acceptance and love from my audience,” Ella said. “I knew I wanted to sing before people the rest of my life.” And that she did. In her lifetime, Ella Fitzgerald won 13 Grammy awards, sold over 40 million albums, and was dubbed “The First Lady of Song.” No wonder she could recover from a forgotten lyric so quickly and turn it into an award-winning performance. Η Cross είχε καταγράψει τα συναισθήματά της για την αλλαγή της δυναμικής στην καριέρα της και το wi…
items.descriptionOriginal: Joan Cross spent 20 years as a passionate art teacher for K-8 grades in the Lakes Region of New Hampshire. But after a noticeable slide in student behavior and other teaching challenges, she decided to make a major career move: to become a commercial truck driver . Cross had been documenting her feelings about changing dynamics in her career and with her students in a personal audio diary. “It was helpful to make those recordings instead of writing things down,” shared in a 2023 interview with New Hampshire Public Radio . Cross offered more details on her audio diary and her decision to leave education for truck driving. “I’m not a school counselor. I’m not a psychologist,” she told NHPR’s Morning Edition host Rick Ganley. “And it felt like those were skills that I needed in order to get through my school day instead of just teaching art.” Cross’s career as an art teacher in changing times In one profound audio diary entry, Cross said: “I’ve spent thousands of dollars and thousands of hours to be an educator. I have a master’s degree. I’ve been doing this for 20 years, and I don’t recognize my profession anymore. Just the social-emotional skill level of these students is unrecognizable. “ Cross added that her classroom and the focus on making art was “falling apart”, noting that following the COVID-19 pandemic, behavioral issues were magnified. “[They were] having emotional issues. I’d have kids wailing, or I’d have kids that are growling at me, literally growling,” Cross added. “They will wreck a room, they’ll just flip a table. And I’m not equipped to help them.” For Cross, choosing to become a truck driver was partly due to diminishing classroom behavior, financial reasons, and overall lack of teacher support. “The pay is not keeping up with the cost of living,” she also shared. “Every time budget season came around, I would glibly be like, ‘Can I have an assistant?’ I need somebody to do all my office work, and all my email correspondence, and help me hang art shows, and label student work and student charts and grades. There’s all this clerical stuff that teachers are doing besides teaching.” Transitioning to truck driving Cross took matters into her own hands. “I earned my Commercial Driver License in 2022 in pursuit of a career change,” Cross wrote on LinkedIn . “My overarching professional goals are: driving a vehicle from a well-maintained fleet in a positive and efficient working environment where safety comes before schedule.” Cross told NHPR that she also decided to pursue her commercial license after growing up driving with her father. “My dad was a retired firefighter, and I just loved any time I got to go on the truck with him,” she explained. “And I like to drive big things.” Much like teaching, being a truck driver also offered Cross an opportunity to serve her community. “[With] teaching you get to serve the community. And whether you’re driving a bus or you’re driving freight, you are helping that community,” she added. “And that is a really, really important piece of my work life.” According to her LinkedIn, she left teaching in June 2023. She went on to train to become a bus driver as a Transit Operator Trainee for Manchester Transit Authority. And as of January 2024, she has been a Transit Driver for the Concord Area Transit (CAT). The post An art teacher left after 20 years to drive trucks. Her audio diary explains why. appeared first on Upworthy .

Το Mac's είναι ένα τοπικό αγαπημένο μπέργκερ. ένα παλιό κατάλυμα που είναι γνωστό για το καλό φαγητό, φτιαγμένο φρέσκο,…
items.descriptionOriginal: Sighle Williams probably never guessed she’d be the star of a big Netflix release. In Gainesville , Florida—far from the glitz and glamour of Hollywood—Williams quietly worked at Mac’s Drive Thru for 37 years before recently deciding to retire. Mac’s is a local favorite burger joint; a throwback establishment that’s known for good food, made fresh, and friendly service. The way things used to be. Mac’s is beloved by its customers but not exactly a viral hotspot that attracts patrons from all over the country. So what brought a documentary crew all the way to Gainesville so they could train their cameras on a humble service worker like Williams? Town organizes a huge retirement surprise for beloved drive-thru worker One of the directors of the upcoming short Netflix documentary One Last Order is Lauren DeFilippo, who just so happens to be the daughter of Mac’s co-owner Ron DeFilippo. So she had a little bit of inside information that let her know there might be a great story sitting right under her nose. Sighle Williams (pronounced Sheila ) was a dedicated and hard-working employee for many years at Mac’s, but she was also so much more. To customers, she was the face of the restaurant, and some even called her the “heart” of Mac’s. She knew nearly every customer by name, and never failed to greet them with a warm smile. Oh, and customers say if she knew your name and face, she’d never forget your order. Customer reviews and comments on the restaurant’s social media pages constantly sing her praises: “When we come to Gainesville … Mac’s is a must. We have had the pleasure of speaking with Sighle during a visit and was a kind and sincere person.” “Always a smile, and she never forgets a face! After my husband died she always took a minute to come speak with me at the window.” “She is amazing! Use to frequent 25 years ago moved away came back and she still remembers me and my order! I was looking for her when pulled in and was so happy to see her smile!” “Definitely one of the best! Soon as she sees me she already know what I’m going to order! Always smiling with such great energy” View this post on Instagram After Williams decided to retire after more than three decades, her boss, DeFilippo, made an incredible gesture: Every dollar spent at Mac’s on Williams’ last day would be donated to her to help kick off her retirement. A lovely idea. But it’s what happened after the announcement of this gesture that truly makes the story documentary-worthy. Not even the directors were prepared to see the snaking line of cars on Williams’ final day of work, clogging up each and every road around Mac’s. The town showed up in huge force that day, with some waiting three hours or more just to be greeted at her window one more time. That’s exactly how much those 30-seconds interactions meant to everyone. The beautiful surprise is not the real story. Williams herself is. The gesture and the town rallying behind Williams make for a poignant climax to a documentary, but even the directors Sam Soko and DeFilippo admit that there’s so much more to the story than just the money raised, and even the community celebrating someone getting their long overdue appreciation. “We went looking for a story and found a practice. Joy, shared daily, with whoever pulls up next. We have carried it with us ever since,” Soko and DeFilippo said in a statement shared with Sinema Focus . Sighle is the star of One Last Order , but she also represents all of the many “Sighles” that live far away from Gainesville, and in every corner of the world. “Everyone has known a Sighle. Sighle is the person who is always, inexplicably, glad to see you, who asks how your mother is doing and then remembers the answer. She is someone who turns the least important stop of your day into the one you look forward to. What neither of us had ever seen was a town line up to say so,” the directors write in a press release. What’s incredible about the story is that it shows us the impact of that everyday kindness. You don’t have to save lives, write policy, or invent new technologies to make a difference in the world. A compliment that brightens someone’s day, lending a genuine ear, or even just sharing a smile. Those are things that people appreciate, and remember. In William’s case, long after the delicious hand-made burger is gone. In the documentary, Williams shares her story with the world for the very first time. Despite her reputation for being a beaming ray of light in the community, she has faced plenty of hardship in her personal life. Williams raised five girls, including her sister and niece’s children, all on her own. Her outward kindness and generosity didn’t happen because it was easy, they happened because Williams made an intentional choice. The filmmakers are hoping that anyone who watches One Last Order will start to make the same choice, or at least appreciate those in our lives who do. “When the credits roll, we leave room for you to think of yours: the bright spot in your week who has no idea the impact they’ve had. We made this so you’d go tell them.” Images from the One Last Order Showing on Sunday, November 22, 2026 at the Heartwood Soundstage in Gainesville, FL. Photo by Matt Pendleton Photography for Insignia Films. Williams told WPLG news that she plans to spend her retirement traveling, fishing, and just enjoying her rest. There’s no doubt that’s she’s earned it. One Last Order premieres on Netflix November 24, 2026. The post She worked a Florida drive-thru for 37 years. On her last day, her boss gave her every dollar customers spent. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Could Smarter Energy Habits Make Outdoor Living More Sustainable? Reading Time: 2 minutes Could Smarter Energy Habits Make Outdoor Living More Sustainable? Picture a weekend camping trip where your devices stay charged, your food stays fresh, and you have everything you need to enjoy a comfortable escape, all without using more energy than necessary. It might sound like a balancing act, but sustainable outdoor living is becoming easier thanks to smarter technology and a few simple changes in how we use energy. Whether you love camping, traveling in an RV, or entertaining in your backyard, your energy habits can have a bigger environmental impact than you might realize. Fortunately, reducing that impact doesn’t have to mean giving up the little comforts that make spending time outdoors so enjoyable. Make Better Use Of Natural Resources Nature already provides some of the resources you need to enjoy outdoor living comfortably. Making the most of natural daylight, for example, can significantly reduce your reliance on artificial lighting. Try planning outdoor activities around daylight hours and positioning your campsite or seating area to maximize natural light. When evening arrives, solar-powered lanterns and energy-efficient LED lights can provide illumination without consuming large amounts of electricity. Solar technology has also made it easier to generate electricity in remote locations, allowing you to enjoy modern conveniences while reducing your dependence on traditional power sources. Choose Smarter Ways To Power Your Adventures Keeping your essential equipment running is often one of the biggest challenges of spending extended periods outdoors. From charging smartphones to powering portable refrigerators, reliable electricity can make your adventures much more comfortable. However, not every activity requires a large generator or constant access to mains electricity. Portable power stations, rechargeable batteries, and solar-compatible equipment can offer practical alternatives. Looking at the equipment available from Power and Pedal can help you find power solutions suited to different outdoor activities . Choosing equipment that matches your energy requirements can reduce unnecessary consumption while ensuring you have sufficient power when you need it. Think Carefully About Your Outdoor Equipment It’s easy to accumulate gadgets and appliances when you enjoy outdoor activities, but not everything needs to be powered by electricity. For example, a well-insulated cooler might be sufficient for a weekend trip, eliminating the need for an electric refrigerator. Similarly, investing in quality thermal clothing and blankets can help you stay comfortable during cooler evenings without relying heavily on electric heating. When electrical equipment is necessary, prioritize energy-efficient models and maintain them properly to extend their lifespan. Plan Ahead To Avoid Wasting Energy Good preparation is one of the simplest ways to improve your outdoor energy habits. Charging devices before leaving home, downloading entertainment for offline use, and checking equipment before traveling can reduce unnecessary power consumption. Planning meals carefully can also help. Preparing ingredients in advance and choosing dishes that require less cooking time can reduce fuel use, especially on longer camping trips. Make Sustainability Part Of Your Outdoor Lifestyle Creating a more sustainable outdoor lifestyle doesn’t require dramatic changes. Often, it’s the smaller decisions that make the greatest difference when repeated consistently. By making thoughtful equipment choices, using renewable energy where practical, and avoiding unnecessary waste, you can reduce your environmental footprint without compromising your enjoyment. The goal isn’t to eliminate energy use entirely. It’s to use the energy you need more efficiently, allowing you to enjoy comfortable outdoor adventures while taking better care of the natural spaces you love exploring. The post Could Smarter Energy Habits Make Outdoor Living More Sustainable? appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: Data from 10,000 workers show sit-stand desks boost active work time by 43 minutes a day—or roughly $9,000 in annual productivity per employee. Every workday is a negotiation between our bodies and our jobs. Sit too long, our backs and necks protest; stand too long, our feet might have something to say about it. Sit-stand desks, also known as height-adjustable desks or standing desks, promise a healthier way to work, giving employees the flexibility to alternate between sitting and standing throughout the day. Now, new research suggests these desks may be giving employees, and employers, another benefit beyond ergonomics and well-being: productivity. Drawing on data from more than 10,000 employees, researchers at Texas A&M University found that workers who used sit-stand desks averaged 43 additional minutes of active computer use each day compared with those using regular desks, a difference that could translate to nearly $9,000 in annual productivity per employee. The study, published in Theoretical and Applied Ergonomics , was co-led by Texas A&M School of Public Health professor Mark Benden and US Army Public Health Command Region, West, Regional Ergonomist Tricia Salzar. The findings suggest that the physical workspace may be a powerful, often overlooked, influence on employee well-being, productivity, and even a company’s overall performance. When organizations look to boost performance and productivity, they turn to new technologies, training programs and management strategies. But another powerful influence may be hiding in plain sight: the physical workplace itself. “It’s what we call the ‘workplace effect,'” Benden says. “The direct impact that the physical work environment has on the behavior, health, psychological well-being, and even engagement and performance of employees.” Sit-stand desks are a striking example of the workplace effect. Rather than locking employees into a single position for hours at a time, they give workers the flexibility to sit, stand and move throughout the day, as tasks and energy levels shift. “It can have a profound effect,” Benden says. “Alternating between different working positions promotes better health outcomes by reducing physical strain and encouraging movement for those who might otherwise spend most of their workday sedentary.” But the benefits may extend beyond physical health. Benden and Salzar’s new research shows that sit-stand desks can also have a substantial impact on productivity. “It has a cumulative, positive effect for both employers and employees,” Benden says. For employees, height-adjustable desks could lead to sustained energy and longer stretches of focused work. For employers, the higher work productivity could translate into a nearly $9,000 return on investment per employee annually. “The implications are hard to ignore,” Benden says. “When we design workplaces around employees and their needs, better health, better performance and better organizational outcomes follow.” The takeaway? Investing in the physical workplace, like height-adjustable desks, isn’t just good for employee comfort and health; it could be good for business, too. To test whether sit-stand desks could influence work output and productivity, Benden and his colleagues stepped out of their labs and turned to the real world, using a resource few ergonomics studies can match. “We analyzed a huge dataset of more than 10,000 workers over a yearlong period, comparing the total computer use of traditional desk users and height-adjustable desk users,” Benden says. The records paired employee comfort surveys with a digital trail of workplace activity, tracking everything from keystrokes and words typed to mouse clicks and typing errors, all to paint a detailed picture of how employees interacted with their computers throughout the workday. “It was important that we collected subjective measurements, like employee survey responses of their comfort and objective measurements of computer activity through software, to analyze how people engaged with their work,” Benden says. The team found that workers with sit-stand desks averaged 3.66 hours of active computer time, compared with 2.95 hours among regular-desk employees—a gap of about 43 minutes a day. That might not sound like much, but over a year it adds up to roughly 171 additional hours, or more than four 40-hour workweeks. And those additional hours come with a practical price tag, too. Multiplying the 171 additional hours by a standardized hourly wage of about $52, the researchers estimate that sit-stand desks could generate nearly $9,000 in potential annual productivity value per employee. “Our findings were exciting because they suggest that height-adjustable desks can directly influence overall work output and economic organizational productivity,” Benden says. The researchers also found that employees using sit-stand desks generally typed more words and logged more keystrokes than their counterparts at non-adjustable desks. “The data showed that people aren’t just engaging with their work, they are producing output in a meaningful way,” Benden says. For Benden, the findings open the door to broader questions about the future of organizations, focusing on another force rapidly reshaping the modern workplace. “Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly integrated into daily work,” Benden says. “Just as we’ve studied how the physical environment affects human health and performance, we’re interested in understanding how emerging AI technologies could influence the physical workspace and outcomes of organizations.” From adjustable desks to emerging technologies, the underlying question remains the same: how can organizations design environments and systems to better support the people who use them? “The next breakthrough may not come from working harder, but from designing workspaces and systems that help people work smarter and more efficiently,” Benden says. The story told by the more than 10,000 employees is that the desk may be doing far more than just holding up your computer. For Benden, sit-stand desks represent more than an ergonomic innovation. They’re part of a lifelong passion to understand how workplaces can be designed to better support employee well-being and organizational success. “We spend a lot of time at work,” Benden says. “It’s my passion to make sure that workers feel supported in their workplace, built on informed and guided scientific evidence.” A former Army Reserve officer, engineer, healthcare professional, inventor and world-renowned researcher, Benden has spent decades studying the complex relationship between people and the environments in which they work. So, the next time you find yourself slumping in your chair at 3pm with an aching back, don’t just reach for another cup of coffee, because the verdict is in: show this study to your boss. Your back—and your company’s bottom line—will thank you. Source: Texas A&M University The post Sit-stand desks boost active work time by 43 minutes a day appeared first on Futurity .

items.descriptionOriginal: Aging is weird. You’re trucking along, enjoying your middle-aged life, finally feeling like a real adult , when you look in the mirror one day and gasp. “Where did those wrinkles come from?” “Is that skin on my arm… crepey ?!?” “Why am I aching like that?” Somewhere in your mid-40s, you start noticing obvious signs of aging that seem to arrive overnight. You assumed it was a gradual process that you just hadn’t noticed, but it sure as heck felt like it happened really fast. The science behind the ‘overnight’ changes Research indicates that may very well be the case. A 2024 study from researchers at Stanford tracked more than 135,000 molecules and microbes in people age 25 to 75 and found that people tend to make two big leaps in aging : one around age 44 and another around age 60. “We’re not just changing gradually over time; there are some really dramatic changes,” said senior study author Michael Snyder, Ph.D., a geneticist and director of the Center for Genomics and Personalized Medicine at Stanford University. “It turns out the mid-40s is a time of dramatic change, as is the early 60s. And that’s true no matter what class of molecules you look at.” The researchers assumed the mid-40s changes would be attributed to menopausal or perimenopausal changes in women influencing the overall numbers, but when they separated the results by sex they saw similar changes in men in their 40s. @suddenly_susan_ The accuracy #40s #genxtiktok #womenover40 #relatable ♬ original sound – Stephaniepisme “This suggests that while menopause or perimenopause may contribute to the changes observed in women in their mid-40s, there are likely other, more significant factors influencing these changes in both men and women. Identifying and studying these factors should be a priority for future research,” said first author Xiaotao Shen , PhD, a former Stanford Medicine postdoctoral scholar who is now an assistant professor at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. Aging happens in bursts, scientists find. Canva Photos What’s behind these bursts? The study included 108 participants who submitted blood and other samples every few months for several years. The scientists tracked age-related changes across all of those molecules and microbes, generating roughly 246 billion data points, to see how aging occurs. The study may shed light on the reasons for jumps in certain diseases and maladies at certain ages. For the 40-somethings, scientists found significant changes in molecules related to alcohol, caffeine, and lipid metabolism, cardiovascular disease, and skin and muscle. For those in their 60s, changes related to carbohydrate and caffeine metabolism, immune regulation, kidney function, cardiovascular disease, and skin and muscle were found. Lifestyle is a factor The study authors did note that lifestyle might play a role in some of these changes. For instance, alcohol metabolism may be influenced by people drinking more heavily in their 40s, which tends to be a period of higher stress for many people. However, the researchers added that these bursts of aging in the mid-40s and early 60s indicate that people may want to pay closer attention to their health around those ages and make lifestyle changes that support greater overall health, such as increasing exercise or limiting alcohol. The research team plans to study the drivers of these aging bursts to find out why they happen at these ages, but whatever the reasons, it’s nice to know that the seemingly sudden onset of age-related woes isn’t just in our imaginations. It’s understandable that we worry about aging, as physical signs of aging remind us of our own mortality. We also have all kinds of social messaging that tells us youth is ideal and beautiful and old is bad and ugly , so of course we give aging the side-eye. But none of us can avoid aging altogether, so the more positive and healthy we are in our approach to aging, the better off we’ll be, no matter when and to what degree aging hits us. This story originally appeared two years ago. It has been updated. The post Study discovers people don’t age steadily, but in dramatic bursts at two specific ages appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: We all know that the level of fitness achieved by celebrities we see on television isn’t attainable for many, if not most, everyday people. And yet, when their sculpted bodies grace our screens, it can still activate a little voice that says “ clearly you’re not doing enough .” That’s why it’s so helpful and grounding when a celebrity is actually transparent about the work it takes to achieve their physique , so that it might quiet that self-deprecating narrative and help us get a little more realistic about achieving whatever fitness goals we might have. Jessica Biel’s response to a fan who asked her to share her workout routine is a perfect example of that. The buzz began with a clip from her Prime Video thriller series The Better Sister , where she plays a super fit character , as is evident by how clearly toned she looks in a backless white dress worn during the show’s opening. It all started with a viral clip Several women have shared the clip on TikTok, while muttering something along the lines of “I need to get back to the gym.” One person even asked Biel to share the workout routine she uses to get that toned. Biel saw the request, and acquiesced… but not without delivering a truth bomb or two. “Everyone is talking… about the white dress… and I just wanted to share that that peak shape in that show is not maintainable unless you are living the strictest, most rigid lifestyle with your nutrition and with your fitness,” she said, admitting that not even she, someone who’s been notably lean and athletic for much of her adult life, who has access to the best foods, best gym equipment, etc. etc., can sustain that look indefinitely. Fans thanked her for keeping it real This bit of candidness incited a whole slew of praise in the comments section, from folks who thanked Biel for “being so real.” “THANK YOU for saying that many if not most actors look amazing for a moment in time during shooting and that it is incredibly hard to enjoy life and look like that all the time,” one person wrote. Another said, “Thank you for speaking about the lifestyle that comes with maintaining! this kind of transparency is so important.” But Biel didn’t stop there. She also took the opportunity to raise awareness on how important it is, especially for women, to prioritize maintaining muscle strength and flexibility as you get older…not just achieving an aesthetic goal, or, for the love of all that is holy, getting skinnier. Here’s the actual workout routine And, as requested, she did end up sharing a sample lower-body workout routine, something she said she was doing at the time to get back in Better Sister shape, which consisted of dumbbell exercises like hip thrusts and Romanian deadlifts, as well as curls with a large stability ball and banded kickbacks. She was even so kind as to break down proper form for all the moves, and didn’t edit out her being out of breath at the end of the routine, saying, “my body’s not twenty years old anymore, you know?” She’s a real one for that. For sure. Biel then concluded her video by saying, “let’s get older and stronger together.” Biel performing a Romanian deadlift as part of her lower body routine. @jessbiel/TikTok The video garnered a lot of gratitude from viewers, who commended Biel for “keeping it real” and “being a great advocate for women.” “JB is a girl’s girl,” one person gushed. At the end of the day, it is possible for us to achieve amazing fitness goals all while juggling what life throws our way. But we are doing ourselves a disservice to think that a) it can be done with a quick fix and zero lifestyle changes, and b) that we are supposed to remain at peak fitness levels 24/7. Not even the pros do that. If getting more fit is a goal of yours, rather than simply stealing Biel’s routine, it might be beneficial to also try to adopt her mindset about it all as well. Just sayin’. Luckily, if you are still on the hunt for a Biel-approved workout, one of her longtime trainers, Ben Bruno, does have fitness programs to try out . (The specific routine featured in this TikTok, though, was taught to her by her Pilates and fitness coach, Ashley Brown.) Here’s to getting older and stronger together. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post Fans gushed over Jessica Biel’s toned body in a white dress. Then she gave a reality check. appeared first on Upworthy .

Ευτυχώς, αυτή δεν είναι η πρώτη φορά που Am…
items.descriptionOriginal: Thanksgiving is right around the corner, and in a year when grocery prices feel like a jump-scare every time we glance at a receipt, many are looking for ways to celebrate without blowing the budget. The American Farm Bureau Federation says a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 now averages $58.63, up 6% from last year. Luckily, this isn’t the first time Americans have had to get creative in the kitchen . During the Great Depression , families all over the country still hosted Thanksgiving dinners, often with barely anything in the pantry. Yet what they managed to whip up wasn’t dreary or depressing. Quite the opposite. These resourceful dishes would be just as flavorful and comforting today as they were decades ago. Here are some Depression-era dishes and tricks that still deserve a spot on a modern Thanksgiving table. Some delicious entrees Swap the turkey for an “old roasted hen” Roasted hen. Photo credit: Canva Turkey was a splurge in the 1930s. The Beaumont Enterprise reported that Thanksgiving dinner for a family of six cost about $5.50, more than 10 hours’ worth of wages for those lucky enough to be working. Many families simply couldn’t justify buying one, so they reached for one of the cheapest roaster birds available: an old hen. As in, past their laying prime, or even roosters. Cooked low and slow with plenty of moisture, it becomes tender and surprisingly rich. Given today’s smaller gatherings and tighter budgets, downsizing the bird might make sense again. Recipe: The Prairie Homestead Mock duck: the original budget workaround One of the most legendary Depression dishes was “mock duck.” Instead of an actual duck, spread flank steak with stuffing, roll it tight, sear it, and roast it until it tastes like something far fancier than it actually is. It’s comfort food cosplay, and it absolutely works. Recipe: BC Food History Stretch the meat with porcupine meatballs Despite the prickly name, porcupine meatballs contain no porcupine . Instead, rice is mixed directly into the meat so it sticks out like little quills. The rice also bulks up the dish so a small amount of meat could feed a crowd. It’s frugal genius. Recipe: Food52 Sides and salads Try classic sides like creamed onions and candied sweet potatoes The long-running USDA radio program Housekeeper’s Chat , hosted by the fictional “Aunt Sammy,” taught home cooks how to stretch every penny. Among its Thanksgiving suggestions: creamed onions, candied sweet potatoes, and simple vegetable dishes built from affordable staples. These sides check every Thanksgiving box: warm, creamy, sweet, and budget-friendly. Recipe: Taste of Home Recipe: The Past is a Foreign Pantry Potato pancakes: the ultimate cheap-and-cheerful staple Potato pancakes. Photo credit: Canva Potatoes were one of the most affordable ingredients of the era, and potato pancakes made frequent holiday appearances. They’re crispy, filling, and perfect for scooping up gravy or topping with applesauce. Recipe: Just a Pinch Don’t sleep on vintage stuffings Chestnut stuffing and apple-and-raisin stuffing, along with a spiced cranberry jelly, were among the Thanksgiving recipes a Beaumont, Texas, newspaper printed in 1932. Sure, some recipes required extra labor, like pressing boiled chestnuts through a sieve, but the flavor payoff was worth it then and now. Recipe: Robin Cutler Recipe: Cardinal Tales Dandelion salad: foraging before it was trendy Many families filled their tables with whatever grew nearby. Dandelion greens, now a fancy “ superfood ,” were a Depression staple. Paired with citrus, eggs, or leeks, they made a fresh, bright starter salad. Recipe: Taste of Home Everyone loves pie For dessert: pumpkin pie or “Hoosier” sugar cream pie Hoosier pie. Photo credit: Canva Fresh pumpkin pie was the go-to, though cooks often used whole pumpkins to avoid the cost of canned puree. And if pumpkins were scarce, families turned to Indiana’s beloved sugar cream pie, sometimes also called a “Hoosier cream pie,” which dates all the way back to the 1800s. It’s simple, silky, and made from pantry basics. What’s not to like? Recipe: Robin Cutler Recipe: Taste of Home The real lesson behind these recipes One thing worth noting: perhaps the even bigger takeaway here is not the recipes themselves, but the mindset of getting back to basics and making the most out of what’s available. And maybe that’s the real inspiration for today. A Thanksgiving table doesn’t need extravagance to be satisfying… or meaningful. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post 8 Depression-era Thanksgiving meal ideas that still hold up today appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: How do you explain the concept of a fourth dimension to humans who are only able to see in 3-D ? Physical space can be measured in height, width, and depth. What is there beyond or in addition to those three dimensions ? How can we understand the existence of a dimension we cannot picture? Thankfully, we had Carl Sagan , one of the greatest science communicators of his time, to help us visualize a fourth dimension. Perhaps best known for his research into extraterrestrial life, Sagan was among the first to demonstrate that life could have existed on Mars. Sagan possessed a unique gift for demystifying complex scientific concepts, making them accessible and thrilling for the general public. He could be described as a scientific Mister Rogers : friendly, a wonderful storyteller, and able to distill difficult lessons into their simplest form. In 1980, on Episode 10 of the groundbreaking PBS show “Cosmos ,” Sagan embarked on a mission to explain the seemingly impossible fourth dimension. It’s a hypnotic, entertaining, and incredibly enlightening watch: Many of us have commonly heard of time being considered the fourth dimension. That’s not so hard to understand. In order to locate an object in the universe, you’d need to know three dimensions of its spatial location and also the time during which it exists. But there is also a more theoretical and harder to understand place, where all four dimensions are spatial. It is nearly impossible for any of us to comprehend… without the help of a gifted teacher. What’s excellent about Sagan’s explanation is that he uses simple and relatable objects: an apple and a tesseract, or hypercube. “In discussing the large-scale structure of the cosmos, astronomers sometimes say that space is curved. Or that the universe is finite but unbound,” Sagan begins. “Whatever are they talking about?” Yeah, this guy gets it. Explaining the third dimension first Sagan then explains how a two-dimensional being living in a flat world would perceive a three-dimensional object like an apple. “Imagine we live in this ‘Flatland’/2-D plane with no concept of ‘up’ or ‘down.’ Then along comes a 3-D object like an apple. We do not even notice it until it crosses our plane of existence, and even then, we have no idea what the apple is,” Sagan explains. “We see only a fragment as it passes through our plane. There is no way we can comprehend the 3-D quality/dimension of the apple, because it is beyond our understanding. We only have the evidence of what has passed through our plane.” Carl Sagan gave many popular lectures. Photo credit: Kenneth C. Zirkel/Wikimedia Commons To further demonstrate, Sagan stamps the apple into an inkpad and then onto the surface in front of him, which represents Flatland and all of its inhabitants. Inside Flatland, the apple exists only as its points of contact on the paper; or four small dots. He adds that as the apple passes through the 2-dimensional Flatland, its cross-section changes. So someone living in that plane of existence would experience the apple as an ever-shifting and rearranging set of shapes or objects. Wild! Enter the mysterious tesseract Sagan then related this two-dimensional experience of the third dimension to how we might try to understand the fourth. To do so, he used the tesseract, a four-dimensional cube, to demonstrate how difficult it is for us to perceive or visualize dimensions beyond our own three. Sagan explains that the tesseract is a cube expanded into a 4th dimension, but “I cannot show you a tesseract because I, and you, are trapped in three dimensions.” But what he can do is show us a 3-dimensional rendering of one. Just like a cube can be drawn and approximated (or cast a shadow) onto a piece of paper, a 4-dimensional tesseract can be imperfectly represented in 3-dimensional space. Still following? At this point, Sagan is asking the viewer to expand their minds to understand the fourth dimension metaphorically. Though we cannot see it or even properly visualize it, that doesn’t mean that the things we can see can’t offer clues and lessons about the fourth dimension. Why this all actually matters Studying 4-dimensional space can help us understand the universe around us. Just because we see and experience only three dimensions doesn’t mean that’s all that exists. It’s critical for physicists and mathematicians to be able to understand and map these theoretical spaces to better comprehend things we otherwise cannot explain. Remember the ever-changing, rearranging set of shapes as the apple passes through Flatland? Sagan’s demonstration of the fourth dimension isn’t just a wonderful explanation of a scientific idea that many of us find difficult to comprehend; it’s also a great example of how to teach complex ideas by combining clear explanations, everyday concepts everyone can understand, and brilliant storytelling. You can check out more of Carl Sagan’s brilliant scientific explanations on the carlsagan.com YouTube channel . This article originally appeared two years ago. It has been updated. items.descriptionOriginal: #thebetterindia **184 trees face the axe in Mumbai. Thousands have objected. But is anyone listening?** 🌳 In Mumbai's Versova, residents once transformed a garbage dump into Nana Nani Park, reclaiming a neglected space and turning it into a green haven for the community. Today, that same park faces an uncertain future, with the proposed felling of **184 trees despite thousands of objections**. At a time when Mumbai is debating the future of its urban green spaces, Bhutan offers a powerful example of what sustainable development can look like. Recognised at the Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai, Bhutan has made environmental conservation central to its vision of progress. Its Constitution mandates that **at least 60% of the country's land remain under forest cover**, reflecting a commitment to protecting nature for future generations. 🌿 The contrast raises an important question: **Can urban development truly be called progress if it comes at the cost of the environment?** As Mumbai continues to expand, the debate surrounding Nana Nani Park highlights a larger challenge facing Indian cities: balancing infrastructure development with environmental protection, climate resilience and public well-being. Urban parks and green spaces are not luxuries. They are essential to cleaner air, healthier communities, biodiversity and a better quality of life. A city can build taller skyscrapers and bigger infrastructure projects, but if its residents lose access to nature, what kind of future is it really creating? **Mumbai's 184 trees are more than just a local environmental issue. They represent a larger conversation about sustainable cities, urban development and the true meaning of progress.** What should come first: rapid urban development or protecting the green spaces that make our cities liveable? **Tell us what you think in the comments.** 🌱 #NanaNaniPark #SaveMumbaiTrees #MumbaiNews #Versova #SaveTrees #Bhutan #EarthshotPrize #SustainableDevelopment #ClimateAction #UrbanGreenSpaces #EnvironmentalConservation #MumbaiEnvironment #GreenCities #ClimateChange #thebetterindia [Mumbai Nana Nani Park, Nana Nani Park Versova, 184 trees Mumbai, Mumbai tree cutting controversy, save Mumbai trees, Versova Nana Nani Park, Mumbai environmental news, Bhutan Earthshot Prize, Earthshot Prize 2026, Bhutan forest conservation, Bhutan 60 percent forest cover, sustainable urban development India, Mumbai green spaces, urban deforestation India, environmental conservation India, climate action India, Mumbai development projects, save trees Mumbai, sustainable cities India, urban green spaces importance, The Better India] “Episode” licensed via Music Vine: FWECZ62E8KJQL3BZ Subscribe Us Now : https://www.youtube.com/thebetterindia Follow us for more: Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/thebetterindia Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/thebetterindia/ Twitter: https://twitter.com/thebetterindia LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/thebetterindia/ Website: https://www.thebetterindia.com/

items.descriptionOriginal: On the night of 26 November 2008, Mumbai Police officer Sanjay Govilkar was shot while helping capture terrorist Ajmal Kasab at Girgaum Chowpatty. Across Mumbai, terrorists were attacking several locations. People across India followed the news from their homes, fearful of what might happen next. Police officers responded across the city, and many lost their lives in the process. Sanjay survived the bullet injury. Years later, he continues to speak about that night, the colleagues he lost, and the work that has filled his life beyond the police force. From writing books to helping families through an NGO he founded with friends, he has found different ways to serve people. The Better India spoke to the former officer about the arrest of Kasab and the experiences that shaped his life afterwards. 'Unfortunately, he never returned' "I consider myself very lucky, as the bullet Kasab fired at me hit the left-hand side of my abdomen and not the right," he smiles. Around the time of the attacks, Sanjay had been excited about the release of his book, Stopwatch . He was going around his colleagues' desks to distribute copies to everyone. Shortly before the attacks began in Mumbai, he visited his boss Hemant Karkare's cabin to give him a copy. "Hemant sir was not there for some reason, so I left a copy for him on his desk. Unfortunately, he never returned," Sanjay recalls. The night he helped capture Kasab alive "As the attack unfolded, we were tense, but we had only one goal: to serve our nation. The moment I heard that my boss, Hemant sir, had been attacked and lost his life, I was upset," he shares. Later that night, Sanjay and his fellow police officers confronted Kasab at Girgaum Chowpatty. During the encounter, Sanjay was shot. "My colleague wanted to immediately shoot him down, but I convinced him to arrest him, as he was a key witness," Sanjay shares. Capturing Kasab alive became an important part of the investigation and trial that followed. Sanjay and his fellow police officers confronted Kasab at Girgaum Chowpatty. During the encounter, Sanjay was shot. "After the arrest, I was immediately rushed to the hospital, where I received treatment for five to six days. I was asked to stay away from the news and was given counselling by a group of doctors. Finally, when I was discharged, I saw that all the noise was settling. My doctors and my family took great care of me," he smiles. The experience left Sanjay with a sense of pride in his service, though he is careful to share the credit with his colleagues. When asked how it feels to have achieved something so significant, he says, "I am extremely proud of serving my country, and I would never want to take advantage of this." He goes on to credit his entire team for the recognition. Why a police officer began writing about health While Sanjay says that being a cop and serving the country was his duty, he was always driven by another passion away from work: writing. Sanjay has so far written and published five books, all of them on health, mental health and relationships. One of those was Stopwatch , the book he had just published when the 26/11 attacks took place. "At one point in my career, I was posted as an immigration officer at the airport and had erratic shifts. This took a toll on my health and prompted me to write the book Stopwatch . It is a must-read for all people who work night shifts," he shares. "I never let my professional experiences shape my writing. I incorporate the lessons I have learnt, but never let them influence my writing," he says. Sanjay maintains clear boundaries between his profession and passion. "I never let my professional experiences shape my writing. I incorporate the lessons I have learnt, but never let them influence my writing," he says. 'My biggest asset is my close friends' His friendships have also shaped another important part of his life. Together with his close friends, Sanjay runs Jeevarang, an NGO inspired by a deeply personal experience. "Twenty-five years ago, I lost my grandmother. She was very dear to me. We cremated her in my village, and the next day, when we visited the site to collect her ashes, we saw dogs feeding on the remains. I was heartbroken by what I saw," he shares. The memory stayed with him and became one of the reasons he wanted to help families give their loved ones a dignified farewell. Through Jeevarang, Sanjay and his friends assist families who have lost their loved ones across 21 villages in Maharashtra. They provide support in cash or kind, depending on what the families need. The NGO began operations in 2007 and also encourages writers by sponsoring the publication of their books. A fraud case that inspired his next chapter Sanjay retired from the police in July 2026. But his interest in helping people facing difficult situations has continued into his retirement. He now runs his own legal and risk advisory firm. The idea goes back to a case he encountered during his police career, involving a mother and daughter who lost their livelihood to online fraud. "I came across a peculiar case in my career in 2009. Online fraudsters tricked a mother and daughter. They were told they had won a lottery and were asked to pay a huge sum of money. The women were innocent and, assuming they would receive a large amount, they sold their small pull-cart shop in Mumbai and lost all their money. The department, however, intervened and cracked the case. This incident stayed with me, and I decided that I wanted to help people who feel stuck in legal issues. That's when I came up with this idea," he shares. The mother and daughter's experience stayed with Sanjay, much like what he had witnessed after his grandmother's cremation years earlier. Both experiences influenced the work he eventually chose to pursue outside policing. When Sanjay speaks about 26/11, he credits his colleagues for what they achieved together. In the years since, he has continued to act on the concerns that have stayed with him, from helping families arrange a dignified farewell to supporting people facing legal difficulties. Individuals seeking guidance or assistance with legal matters and risk-related concerns can find information about the services offered by Govilkar Legal & Risk Advisory on its official website . The firm aims to help people understand complex legal situations and consider their next steps.
